summary: Human, food, paint, razor, blood and animal themes all fit poisoning. Person or theme changes do not establish separate lexical senses. The cat episode is an attempted attack on humans whose food kills a test animal; the quotation does not establish that all humans ingested poison.
Detransitive patient-state clauses suppress the agent; 60/243 is an event after drinking, blood-analysis clauses deny contamination, and Part. Pass. forms combine with copulas or modify nouns.

Part act. msammoniṯo/msammone expresses poisonous capacity; Part. Pass. msamamto/msammo/msamme expresses treated or contaminated state. The existing Part act. example includes a finite Preterit as co-text but its target is msammoniṯo; no wholesale box move is justified.

The supplied entry has three Preterit and two Infectum examples, not the inflated reader counts. One Detransitive Preterit example was present with a bad citation and missing-example note. Repairs and additions use those actual baseline counts.
The proposed Detransitive sense 1 heading makes explicit the meaning already implicit in existing boxes; reader D1 labels are represented as sense 1 with detransitive=true and canonical box labels.
Does mi- in misamәm (Lahdo The snake/7) establish Detransitive Infectum rather than a vowel-expanded state form? The added form is provisional.
What is the referent of i+məssine in MAC NI Sultan and barber/11, translated pitcher where adjacent instructions mention a razor? No pitcher-specific sense or example is added.
Confirm contracted msamamne and the -on- derivation of venomous msammone. Retain glossary Part act. terminology pending editorial analysis.
For the poisoned horse, does the adjective describe application of poison making contact dangerous, contamination of the animal, or both? No illness of the horse itself is asserted.
Part act. poisonous property extends from coffee to a lethal gift and venomous snakes; no new numbered sense required.
